text.p: Primetown Property Group Inc said on Monday its net income rose to 175 million pesos from 81 million pesos posted in the same period last year.
The firm said in a statement that revenues from January to March rose to 713 million pesos from 359 million in the same period last year.
The increase in first quarter net was due to the completion of a hotel on the island resort of Boracay in the central Philippines and other projects, the firm said.

"Primetown shall continue to be a beneficiary of the economic boom as long as the country remains on track in its march towards achieving a newly industrialised status by the year 2000," Primetown chairman Kenneth Yap said.

The firm popularised condominium hotels called "condotels" in the Philippines, a new marketing concept which enabled property owners to combine condominium ownership into an investment package by offering their units into a pooled hotel operation managed by international hoteliers.
